title: SBQ: Exploiting Significant Bits for Efficient and Accurate Post-Training DNN Quantization
problem: Post-training quantization below 4-bit encounters severe accuracy degradation due to high clipping/rounding errors from limited quantization levels and narrow data range, especially for attention-based LLMs.
motivation: Aggressive quantization (2-4 bits) is crucial for inference efficiency, but conventional PTQ methods fail to maintain accuracy at extreme bit-widths.
method: SBQ enables extreme low-precision quantization (2-4 bits) without accuracy loss by extracting only significant bits—the most critical bits—from high-precision operands. A product-aware method identifies which bits matter by examining multiplication results. Error-compensated computation mathematically corrects for the discarded bits, and a custom inference engine efficiently implements this on hardware.
key_novelty: Dynamically extracting significant bits (the most critical bits) and mathematically compensating for the discarded bits enables accurate quantization at extreme compression levels (2-4 bits).
contributions: Outperforms prior PTQ methods under 2-4 bit quantization on CNNs, ViTs, and LLMs
Dedicated inference engine with high area and energy efficiency
Competitive with bit-operation quantization architectures (TQ, Sibia)

metrics.other: highest area and energy efficiency vs TQ and Sibia

limitations: Training overhead and cost of dynamic bit selection not discussed; applicability to sparse or pruned models unclear.
primary_theme: significant-bit extraction for extreme low-bit quantization
